pairs.subject: error-handling
pairs.evidence: src/lib/utils/apiError.ts:55 classifyError keeps its own prose TRANSIENT/PERMANENT pattern lists for retry policy beside src/lib/errorTaxonomy.ts:4 (declared TS single source of truth), so retry and user copy classify one failure independently and can drift

techniques.evidence: src/lib/utils/apiError.ts:55 a second frontend classifier (severity from prose patterns) independent of src/lib/errorTaxonomy.ts:4, which tells subsystems to import from it instead of maintaining independent heuristics

src/lib/utils/apiError.ts:57 the app's own InvokeTimeoutError (src/lib/tauriInvoke.ts:134, a typed class carrying backendMayStillBeRunning) has no instanceof branch and is rediscovered as transient from its message text; kind-first path (:146) and cause preservation (:33) are otherwise realized
src/lib/utils/crashPersistence.ts:111 sanitizes before the first write, local spool bounded at :36, spool parsed defensively at :122, backend shipping fire-and-forget at :157

src/lib/utils/staleWhileRevalidate.ts:135 background revalidation failure routed through silentCatch; src/lib/utils/tauri/safeInvoke.ts:80 fallback only for the declared unregistered-command probe, everything else rethrown
src/lib/utils/parseJson.ts:26 the one empty catch is visibly declared intentional, and the module offers the error-returning safeJsonParse beside it
src/lib/utils/apiError.ts:195 the context only extracts raw messages; the copy registry lives in src/lib/errors/errorRegistry.ts outside this context

pairs.registryProposal: lib-utils is a consolidated grab-bag (cron presets, animation, crash persistence, fetch caches, apiError); error-handling governs only 5 of its 17 files, so a whole-context verdict is driven by apiError.ts. Consider letting conform verdicts scope to a file subset for consolidated contexts.
